covers: INT 10h AH=12h, the alternate function select of the video BIOS: the call and its variants chosen by BL.

rows.text: Alternate function select: BL picks the function, and only an EGA, VGA or MCGA machine answers.
A BL that no variant handles leaves AL set to 0, except on an EGA machine.
With BH=55h on an ATI VGA, BL up to 6 is looked at first: 2 stores a status in AL, 6 sets ES:BP to fixed values, the rest are logged.
Before the dispatch the cursor of the DOS-V or Japanese display is turned off and the current mode is read from the BIOS data.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12; BL then picks the variant.

searched.gave: Not applicable: the DOSBox-X source header cites no document.
IBM's PS/2 BIOS Interface Technical Reference is named by third-party pages; no maker-hosted copy was seen.
One search listed a scan of System BIOS for IBM PC XT AT; no scan of a VGA BIOS interface manual.
One web search listed mirrors of Ralf Brown's list and a VGABIOS.TXT; no maker document for the family dispatch.

rows.text: Alternate function select, get EGA information, on PS, EGA, VGA and MCGA.
BL is 10h.
BH is the video state: 00h color mode in effect, I/O port 3Dxh; 01h mono mode, port 3Bxh.
BL is the installed memory: 00h 64K, 01h 128K, 02h 192K, 03h 256K.
CH holds the feature connector bits.
CL holds the switch settings.
With BH set to FFh before the call, BH comes back unchanged if no EGA or later card is present.
Feature connector bits 0 to 3 are the FEAT 1 and FEAT 0 lines in states 2 and 1; bits 4-7 are unused.
Switch setting bits 0 to 3 are switches 1 to 4 OFF; bits 4-7 are unused.
Switch setting values 00h to 0Bh name the primary and secondary display of the original EGA or VGA.
On an MCGA machine the call is not answered: BH, BL and CX stay as they were.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, alternate print screen, on PS, EGA, VGA and MCGA.
BL is 20h, to select the alternate print screen routine.
Nothing is returned.
It installs a PrtSc routine from the video card's BIOS in place of the ROM BIOS one, which does not understand screens of other than 25 lines.
Some adapters disable print screen instead of enhancing it.
No print screen routine is installed: the case does nothing.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, select vertical resolution, on VGA.
BL is 30h.
AL is the vertical resolution: 00h 200 scan lines, 01h 350, 02h 400.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It sets the number of scan lines used to display text modes.
The resolution takes effect on the next mode set.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
With an SVGA card an AL above 2 returns AL=0 and changes nothing else.
With no SVGA card an AL above 2 acts as 0 but leaves the mode-set bit.
The call reads the mode-set control and the video switches bytes of the BIOS data first.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, palette loading, on VGA and MCGA.
BL is 31h.
AL is the new state: 00h enable default palette loading, 01h disable it.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It specifies whether a default palette is loaded when the display mode is set.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
An AL above 1 returns AL=0, an invalid subfunction, and changes nothing else.
With a Tseng ET4000 card only bit 0 of AL counts.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, video addressing, on VGA and MCGA.
BL is 32h.
AL is the new state: 00h enable video addressing, 01h disable it.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It specifies whether the CPU can reach video memory and the adapter's I/O registers.
The AL state is only checked, never applied: the call logs that it is not handled.
The CPU's access to video memory and the I/O registers is not changed.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
With a Tseng ET4000 card only bit 0 of AL counts.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, gray-scale summing, on VGA and MCGA.
BL is 33h.
AL is the new state: 00h enable gray-scale summing, 01h disable it.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It specifies whether colors are converted to gray scale when palette or color registers are loaded.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
An AL above 1 returns AL=0, an invalid subfunction, and changes nothing else.
With a Tseng ET4000 card only bit 0 of AL counts.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, cursor emulation, on VGA.
BL is 34h.
AL is the new state: 00h enable alphanumeric cursor emulation, 01h disable it.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It specifies whether the BIOS remaps the cursor start and end by the character height in text modes.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
An AL above 1 returns AL=0, an invalid subfunction, and changes nothing else.
With a Tseng ET4000 card only bit 0 of AL counts.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, display-switch interface, on PS.
BL is 35h.
AL is the subfunction: 00h initial adapter video off, 01h initial planar video on, 02h active video off, 03h inactive video on, 80h undocumented.
ES:DX points to a 128-byte save area when AL is 00h to 03h.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It switches between two video adapters whose addresses may conflict.
No subfunction is carried out: the call logs that it is not handled.
The save area at ES:DX is never read or written.
No adapter is switched.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
Alternate function select, video refresh control, on PS and VGA.
BL is 36h.
AL is the new state: 00h enable refresh, 01h disable it.
AL is 12h if the function is supported.
It specifies whether video memory is displayed; disabling refresh blanks the screen.
With refresh disabled the whole screen shows the color of DAC register 00h, so to blank it set that to black first.
On a machine that is not VGA architecture the call does nothing and AL is unchanged.
With an S3 Trio card an AL above 1 returns AL=0 and changes nothing else.
The call reads sequencer register 1, changes its bit 5 and writes it back.
The INT 10h handler reaches it by its case 0x12 and then by BL.
